title: Annotatio II §.VII close: After Berengar’s public censure; consub born from over-fighting him; stop before §.VIII
pass_a_gloss: After the Berengarian sentence — to which the Consubstantiators had openly opposed themselves, and in excessive fighting of which they had begotten their Consubstantiation — had already then suffered public censure in Berengar’s own person. Of which there will be a more convenient place of speaking in the following Annotations.
pass_b_english: By then Berengar’s sentence had already taken public censure in his person.
Consubstantiators had openly fought him — and in over-fighting him had begotten their own Consubstantiation.
More on that in the Annotations that follow.
Stop before §.VIII (PERDURATIO / revival after apparent extinction).
source_text: Postquam jam tum Berengariana sententia, cui sese Consubstantiatores ex professo opposuerant, inque nimia ejus oppugnatione Consubstantiationem suam progenuerant, in ipsa Berengarii persona censuram publicam passa fuisset. Quo de in sequentibus Annotationibus commodior dicendi locus fuerit.

rejected: in a nimiety of oppugnation slang

notes: Berengar censure; over-fight begets consub; stop §.VIII.
